claim: Riot ranks correcting inaccurate/missing hitbox indicators and wrong communication first, visibility/noise/visual power second, theme third. Skin variants retain the corrected indicator size. Feedback should identify a specific actionable issue.
limitations: A League production policy, not an experimental comparison or numerical tolerance.

claim: Importance reflects damage, crowd control, dodgeability and influence on play. Projectile direction should remain readable without motion. Champion recognition and clarity parity survive skins; effects are checked across maps.
limitations: No universal layer count, luminance ratio, particle count or screen-coverage limit.

claim: Designers assign importance from 1–10 for caster, enemies and allies. Morgana’s R range circle is omitted for allies who cannot act on it. League conventions include green nonthreatening heals, vertical knockups and floor-ring/cylinder roots.
limitations: Conservative C classification follows the brief’s forum category despite first-hand maker provenance. S02 corroborates hierarchy; S16 corroborates viewer-dependent variants. The exact 1–10 scale has no second independent source located.

claim: The damaging missile head is primary; thematic trail is secondary. Contrast, saturation and shape differentiation support focus and rest.
limitations: Corroborated by original Riot guide S05 and official Riot S02; not an eye-tracking experiment.

claim: Guide covers truthful gameplay geometry, primary/secondary hierarchy, value, colour, shape and timing. Its charts are schematic, with no numeric interior ranges. It discourages 0%/100% value/saturation and demotes outros.
limitations: PRE-2020. Original Riot PDF URL currently redirects. Mirror linked from original release thread https://realtimevfx.com/t/official-league-of-legends-vfx-style-guide/3392 by a community poster on 2026-10-06; not an authenticated studio reissue. No exact RGB or luminance target can be read from the schematic bars.

claim: Summarizes the guide’s focal hierarchy, restrained palettes, mixed hard/soft shapes, directional blur, anticipation and short linger.
limitations: A secondary teaching summary. Corroboration: S05 original, S01/S02 modern Riot. The statement about effects assisting story is the teacher’s framing, not a universal film rule.

claim: Faint, desaturated wispy placeholders failed in busy Sparkball play. Hall used broad, crisp, bolder shapes. Main action usually finishes or starts dissipating in the first quarter of lifetime; an expiring stun trap intentionally blinks out.
limitations: Firsthand Sparkball account; exact first-quarter heuristic is not independently validated and is excluded from universal defaults.

claim: Lists gameplay, shape, value, color, timing and composition. The composition lesson explicitly connects VFX to posters, comics and thumbnails.
limitations: Use for terminology and syllabus only; no experimental claims or unpublished lesson specifics. Principles corroborated by S02/S05/S09.

claim: Applies animation principles to real-time effects, blocks key poses before detail, offsets secondary timing and tests in-game context. One explosion revision adds 2–3 smaller outward-moving sprites after the initial sprite.
limitations: PRE-2020. Counts describe examples, not budgets. Skipping 7–8 frames was an attempted demonstration that failed to solve the whole effect; it is not a recommendation.

claim: Simple grayscale textures, shaders and meshes expose timing and composition. Retiming the same block-in changes its apparent friendly/damaging character; polished colour and dissolves are not required to inspect punch.
limitations: A teaching demonstration, not controlled research. Corroboration: Lyndon S09 and Hall S07.

claim: Curriculum uses windup, crescendo, follow-through and dissipation, and includes block-ins and kitbashing.
limitations: Terminology and scope only; no phase milliseconds or recommended emitter counts. S09 corroborates phase-led workflow.

claim: Distinguishes impulse/crescendo and flowing/disruptive rhythm; recommends timing charts and simple block-ins. It notes instant effects can omit windup under gameplay constraints.
limitations: The article’s heal-below-60-BPM heuristic has no independent support found and is excluded from agent defaults. Block-in approach corroborated by S09/S10.

claim: Attention depends jointly on features, goals, history, reward and scene meaning. Target–distractor differences and distractor similarity influence guidance. The paper models selection around 20 Hz; it is not a VFX display-rate prescription.
limitations: Theory/review, not a Roblox gameplay trial. Do not turn approximate attentional-selection timing into a minimum warning duration.

claim: Motion onset impaired unique-shape search, but was avoided when observers searched for a prescribed shape. Experiment 1: n=24, 1057 vs 998 ms, d=.41; Experiment 2: n=24, 560 vs 557 ms, p=.436, d=.026.
limitations: Laboratory rotating shapes; no effect-strength or notification-duration recommendation. Motion is not an unconditional attention magnet.

claim: 50 observers; 13 crowding distances measured twice. Two-parameter eccentricity model explained 82% cross-validated variance; augmented model 94%. Thresholds vary by position, orientation, target type and observer.
limitations: Letter recognition under fixation; no permissible particle count, phone pixel gap, or universal screen-coverage percentage follows.

claim: Allies see updated Mythic effects while enemy-facing identity remains recognizable. The team preserves gameplay/performance and texture-memory constraints.
limitations: Qualitative maker practice; no engine-independent memory or layer budget.

claim: Similar-value materials limit environment noise; gameplay spaces are illuminated; most ornamental details sit above player height. The team playtests maps weekly during modeling.
limitations: FPS environment guidance. Above-player-height staging does not directly transfer to a top-down camera; apply the sightline principle instead.

claim: Separates correct simulation from misleading feedback. Muzzle/tracer presentation begins at least one rendered frame after input; confirmed hits wait for server round-trip. Example 40 ms one-way produces 80 ms plus processing delay.
limitations: Historical VALORANT implementation example, not a Roblox latency guarantee or recommendation. Proposed fixes in article must not be claimed shipped.

claim: Abstract scenes with short angular nonhorizontal contours were judged more threatening; smooth long horizontal contours safer. Experiments 2a/2b each n=157. Natural-photo regression explained R²=.04 overall, .08 for far scenes.
limitations: Feature combinations matter; effects in still scenes do not prove universal circle/triangle/square meanings or game enjoyment.

claim: 4598 participants in 30 nations/22 languages associated 20 emotions with 12 colour terms. Mean pattern similarity r=.88; linguistic/geographic proximity further shaped associations.
limitations: Colour-word association survey, not proof a rendered hue causes an emotion or that a game trope is universal.

claim: n=71; looming animals modulated early attention-related ERPs with emotion/distance interactions. Motion effect on P1p at 140 ms: partial η²=.113; N2po at 280 ms: .287. Behavioral reaction-time main effect of motion was nonsignificant(p=.087).
limitations: Stereoscopic animals and line task, not explosions. Do not claim looming always worsens performance or makes threats detectable within 140 ms.

claim: Abrupt distractors reduced probe detection without generally reducing tracking performance; rapid serial onsets did impair tracking. Lower onset frequency increased capture.
limitations: Abstract-level evidence only; no safe recurrence interval or maximum effect count extracted.

claim: Set the review goal, make feedback specific and suggest a solution; prioritize changes that serve the project.
limitations: Corroboration: official Riot S01 actionable-feedback guidance. No tested optimal review cadence.

claim: Verified session exists and addresses information overload, integration with design and directing attention.
limitations: Discovery-only for detailed methods: no numeric budgets or specific fixes attributed to unwatched talk.

claim: Verified speaker/year/title. Abstract mentions rhythm, balance, negative space and a first-pass-effect demonstration.
limitations: Do not confuse this 2026 design talk with Disney’s 12 animation principles or claim its examples were inspected.

claim: Keller identifies fewer simultaneous actors/VFX as cognitively easier to track while acknowledging that greater chaos can create appealing peaks.
limitations: Historical trade-off discussion; 9vs 11 other players is not a perceptual capacity threshold or a current-mode status claim.

claim: Observational game comparison describes directional shake, camera focus, slow motion and hit-stop. Guilty Gear Xrd -SIGN- examples use 7 frames for light hits and about 10 for heavy hits; Dragon Ball FighterZ has an approximately 1-second ultimate hold.
limitations: Examples, not optimum timings. No verified capture frame rate conversion or causal camera-feature effect size. User-comment rankings and feature inventories cannot establish that a specific feature caused impact feel. Duplicate of studies module JS03.

claim: ParticleEmitter Rate is documented up to 400 particles/second per emitter, or 100/second on mobile.
caveat: Not scene-wide live-particle count; not a safe operating budget; do not infer an Emit burst cap from this statement.

claim: The particle tutorial documents Lifetime values internally capped at 20 seconds.
caveat: Do not use this as a desirable effect duration. TimeScale affects effect time; cleanup must account for freezing/slowing.

claim: FlipbookFramerate is a NumberRange with documented maximum 30 frames/second.
caveat: OneShot ignores this property; it is not a universal display-frame-rate ceiling.

claim: Standard layouts have 4, 16 or 64 cells (2×2, 4×4, 8×8); Custom uses FlipbookSizeX/Y.
caveat: Not an aesthetic optimum or universal mobile budget.

claim: The 2025 custom-layout announcement specifies integer row and column counts from 1 to 64 and removes square/power-of-two texture restrictions.
caveat: Original announcement title still says Client Beta. Current Creator Docs independently list Custom; verify imported assets on target clients.

claim: OneShot distributes its sheet cells evenly across Lifetime; Loop repeats; PingPong reverses; Random samples random frames.
caveat: Not an aesthetic optimum or universal mobile budget.

claim: Frame blending is linear crossfade or immediate frame replacement; in modes honoring framerate, random start plus 0 fps can select static random sheet frames.
caveat: Not an aesthetic optimum or universal mobile budget.

claim: LightEmission 0 means normal blending and 1 additive; it does not illuminate geometry. LightInfluence 0–1 controls environmental lighting.
caveat: Not an aesthetic optimum or universal mobile budget.

claim: Particle Brightness scales appearance when LightInfluence is 0; ZOffset moves render depth in studs without changing projected size; positive offsets approach camera.
caveat: Not an aesthetic optimum or universal mobile budget.

claim: Positive Squash narrows horizontally and stretches vertically; negative does the reverse. TimeScale runs from 0 frozen to 1 normal. Emit(n) spawns a burst; Clear removes current particles.
caveat: Not an aesthetic optimum or universal mobile budget.

claim: A Beam needs at least n−1 segments for n color/transparency keypoints; Segments defaults to 10.
caveat: If color and transparency have different keypoint counts, satisfy the larger requirement. More segments is not automatically visually better.

claim: Beam.TextureSpeed is texture cycles/second, not studs/second. Beam Brightness allows 0–10000, default 1, affected by LightInfluence.
caveat: Do not transplant Beam Brightness limits onto ParticleEmitter without its own source.

claim: Trail Lifetime is 0.01–20 seconds, default 2. MaxLength=0 is unlimited by distance; WidthScale is a 0–1 multiplier of attachment separation.
caveat: Not an aesthetic optimum or universal mobile budget.

claim: Highlight has 255 simultaneous client slots; disabled instances still consume slots and excess instances are ignored.
caveat: Older 31-instance advice is stale. A slot limit is not a recommended count.

claim: PointLight, SpotLight and SurfaceLight Range is capped at 120 studs. ExtendLightRangeTo120 is unused.
caveat: Older 60-stud advice is stale; the obsolete rollout switch cannot expand the clamp.

claim: Lighting.Technology is deprecated; LightingStyle and PrioritizeLightingQuality are the current controls.
caveat: Do not use the 2025 announcement’s scriptability statement as a current guarantee; current API metadata has changed.

claim: Post effects can differ or disappear at low graphics quality and do not affect GuiObjects.
caveat: A gameplay-critical signal must remain readable without the post effect; this requirement is our inference.

claim: ColorGradingEffect works only under Lighting; multiple instances do not combine and the latest-parented instance wins.
caveat: Not an aesthetic optimum or universal mobile budget.

claim: Camera FieldOfView is clamped to 1–120 degrees with default 70.
caveat: These are not recommended shake or zoom values; source warns extreme FOV can disorient.

claim: Engine QualityLevel has 21 explicit levels plus Automatic; SavedQualitySetting has 10 explicit levels plus Automatic.
caveat: No reliable universal level-to-particle-count or level-to-post-effect mapping; behavior is device/platform-specific.

claim: General Roblox texture documentation allows up to 4096×4096, but the same page retains a 1024×1024 UV-map statement.
caveat: Do not promise effective 4K ParticleEmitter pixels. Import allowance, downloaded mip and rendered quality are different facts.

claim: Texture streaming currently lists ParticleEmitter and Beam among supported types; whole-atlas detail is loaded when one area requires it.
caveat: Trail is not in the page’s supported-type list; absence does not prove a permanent engine limitation.

claim: Large particle screen area and overlapping transparency increase GPU cost. Low memory can automatically disable flipbooks.
caveat: No universal allowed screen percentage, overlap count or safe total particle count found.

claim: 1024×1024 has four times as many pixels as 512×512; upload disk compression/grayscale is not a promised Roblox graphics-memory saving.
caveat: Runtime transcoding, streaming and device resources determine actual resident memory.

claim: Roblox default target is 60 FPS, corresponding to 16.67 ms/frame.
caveat: This is the entire frame budget, not a VFX-only allowance.

claim: Roblox recommends 10–15 minutes of active mobile play to expose thermal throttling.
caveat: Not an aesthetic optimum or universal mobile budget.

claim: The design guide’s 1000 draw calls and 1000000 triangles are an illustrative device-derived example, not a universal Roblox threshold.
caveat: Not an aesthetic optimum or universal mobile budget.

claim: Jason Keyser recommends supplementary particles and 3D elements around a flipbook, guided by use context and frequency.
caveat: No optimal layer count or variant count is supplied.

claim: Kirill Anchikov’s Flame Burst uses an 8×4 sheet suited to an elongated 1:2 frame and combines it with other VFX elements.
caveat: Case example, not Roblox performance validation or an optimal grid.

claim: At fixed playback, cell duration=L/N seconds; effective OneShot rate=N/L. For an atlas W×H, cell dimensions are W/columns by H/rows before padding.
caveat: Formula, not an empirically validated feel prescription; actual display sampling may skip frames.

claim: At 24 presentation fps, on 2s means 12 unique-frame updates/second; at 60 presentation fps it means 30.
numeric_context: arithmetic from explicitly stated presentation cadence
caveat: The 24-fps example defines an illustrative reference cadence, not a Roblox recommendation. Record the intended reference cadence instead of equating all on-2s work to 12 fps.

claim: An uncompressed RGBA8 base image would require width×height×4 bytes; an ideal full mip pyramid tends to 4/3 of base.
caveat: Assumes 4 bytes/texel and ideal mip chain; not observed Roblox GPU memory. Use measured client memory for acceptance.

claim: Truthful indicator before ornament (League); Intended to make attack extent and identity legible.
evidence_level: Industry practice; game transfer is inference

claim: Environment as a contrast budget (VALORANT); Intended to keep opponents and action separable from scenery.
evidence_level: Industry practice; game transfer is inference

claim: Observer-specific cosmetic treatment (Overwatch 2); Intended to retain opponent recognition while allowing allied spectacle.
evidence_level: Industry practice; game transfer is inference

claim: Combined-system review (Rocksteady); Avoiding overload is a stated production goal; no measured effect size.
evidence_level: Industry practice, abstract only; proposed review is inference

claim: Beat-aligned action with responsive exceptions (Hi-Fi RUSH); Creator intends rhythmic hits to feel musically forceful.
evidence_level: Industry practice; game transfer is inference
numeric_context: 60 FPS production target reported; no universal impact delay found

claim: Tactile shader iteration (Balatro); Creator associates tactile treatment with a coherent aesthetic; no causality test.
evidence_level: Industry practice; game transfer is inference

claim: Boldness over negligible detail (Hades); Artist intended immediate, visceral, satisfying work.
evidence_level: Documented intention only; operational transfer is inference

claim: Destruction changes available routes (Teardown); Player reads destruction as an actionable world change.
evidence_level: Industry practice; game transfer is inference

claim: Prefractured authored structure plus runtime consequences (THE FINALS); Makes breakage belong to a traversable building, rather than arbitrary spray.
evidence_level: Industry practice; game transfer is inference

claim: Damage-edge restraint (THE FINALS); Studio intended more accurate judgment of damage.
evidence_level: Industry practice; game transfer is inference

claim: Material event drives VFX and sound (Battlefield 6); Intended material identity and coherent impact response.
evidence_level: Industry practice; game transfer is inference

claim: Staged damage with usable ruins (Battlefield 6); Makes damage progression and remaining cover interpretable.
evidence_level: Industry practice; game transfer is inference

claim: Gameplay destruction separated from cosmetic debris (Rainbow Six); Supports convincing breakage without making every fragment gameplay-critical.
evidence_level: Industry practice; game transfer is inference
numeric_context: 2016 slides report title-specific budgets, not adopted here; no portable debris count found

claim: Held graphic poses with anti-strobing treatment (Spider-Verse); Studio intended distinct illustrated images and speed clarity.
evidence_level: Industry practice; game transfer is inference
numeric_context: At 24 fps, ones=24 unique images/s, twos=12. Across uses 1s–6s; holds are artistic, not a game-FPS mandate.

claim: Reusable elements versus bespoke hero design (Spider-Verse); Reused components provide efficiency; bespoke drawings improve shot fit per makers.
evidence_level: Industry practice; game transfer is inference

claim: Poof breakup preserves silhouette (Turning Red); Intended to retain a designed graphic appearance while dissipating.
evidence_level: Industry practice; game transfer is inference

claim: Coherent sprite/simulation hybrid (The Bad Guys); Audience is meant to perceive one graphic effect, not separate media.
evidence_level: Industry practice; game transfer is inference

claim: Stepped action plus controlled figure/background separation (Puss); Maker intends snappy poses and readable characters.
evidence_level: Industry practice; game transfer is inference

claim: Character-state graphic overlays (Arcane); Graphic overlays communicate subjective character experience.
evidence_level: Industry practice; game transfer is inference

claim: Coarse-to-fine motion layers (Dune); Makers intend vast scale and believable granular motion.
evidence_level: Industry practice; game transfer is inference

claim: Captured ingredients re-timed and composited (Oppenheimer); Makers seek photographic richness and designed impact.
evidence_level: Industry practice; game transfer is inference

claim: Material-appropriate deformation (Godzilla Minus One); Preserves identity of what is being destroyed.
evidence_level: Industry practice; game transfer is inference

claim: Human-scale framing and destructive sequence staging (Godzilla); Director intends fear and scale.
evidence_level: Industry practice; game transfer is inference

claim: Designed water vocabulary and hybrid shot construction (Demon Slayer); Gives attacks a distinctive illustrated elemental identity.
evidence_level: Industry practice; game transfer is inference

claim: Exaggerate reference selectively (Chainsaw Man artist example); Artist strengthens action silhouette beyond literal cloth behavior.
evidence_level: Industry practice; game transfer is inference

claim: Graphic impact insert (Kameda); Artist uses strong black/white imagery for visual force.
evidence_level: Maker testimony; game transfer is inference; no validated intensity/timing prescription

claim: Sparse focal contrast with localized following emitters (Beyond the Dark); Creators intend eyes and tentacle tips to hold attention.
evidence_level: Documented sample practice + platform specification; no efficacy experiment

claim: Goal movement against a quiet scene (Island Jump); Tutorial intends to draw players toward the objective and give air depth.
evidence_level: Official illustrative tutorial / Spec; game transfer is inference

claim: Truthful gameplay signaling is the first production priority; decorative theme follows.
limitations: No numerical readability thresholds established.

claim: Map art is deliberately simplified and tested around player visibility.
limitations: Environment policy does not guarantee effect legibility on its own.

claim: Mythic skin presentation can differ by observer relationship.
limitations: Do not infer different hitboxes or damage indicators are acceptable.

claim: Public session framing addresses combined-system readability.
limitations: Abstract-only supplemental case, not a fully reconstructed production method.

claim: Rhythmic action and clean graphic rendering were explicit design goals.
limitations: Do not generalize its musical timing to non-rhythm combat.

claim: Creator describes tactile shader exploration and iterative juice.
limitations: Case establishes intention, not exactly how much shake, shader distortion or delay is effective.

claim: Credited artist documents a deliberate move toward bold immediate expression.
limitations: Detailed current maker evidence for Hades VFX construction is insufficient in this pass.

claim: Destruction is a route-planning and heist-execution mechanic, not merely an explosion layer.
limitations: No attempt here to recreate its voxel solver or claim sprite VFX provide equivalent destruction.

claim: Authored prefractured buildings retain interior/collision quality; damage presentation is tuned for accurate judgment.
limitations: A prefractured asset is not proof that every break is scripted; physical collapse and authoring are separate stages.

claim: Systemic breakage is shaped to leave playable ruins, with material-aware VFX/audio emission.
limitations: Event schema proposed below is our synthesis, not copied engine architecture.

claim: Classic implementation distinguishes procedural wall damage and lightweight decorative fragments.
limitations: 2016 technical details cannot be assumed unchanged in Siege X; 2025 source confirms only ongoing strategic environmental destruction.

claim: Reusable graphic ingredients and stepped motion are documented; sequel increased bespoke shot work.
limitations: Per-component film cadence is not a license to desynchronize gameplay/contact; art-directed camera privileges do not automatically transfer.

claim: Graphic poofs use designed breakup; other hand-painted elements avoid simulation entirely.
limitations: Replaying a breakup texture approximates authored appearance; it does not implement Pixar’s subdivision or fluid tools.

claim: Library sprites and procedural work share an intentionally illustrated visual vocabulary.
limitations: Do not assume merely stacking sprites hides the medium boundary automatically.

claim: Action timing, lighting and background simplification were coordinated.
limitations: No one cadence applies to the whole film; article describes stepped action but supplies no universal frame count.

claim: Drawn overlays complement shot-led animation and graphic composition.
limitations: Do not call all Arcane effects 2D or claim a uniform stepped rate from this source.

claim: Layered coarse motion and fine granular/dust detail sell worm-driven sand displacement.
limitations: This recipe is a visual approximation; it cannot reproduce interactive sand volume or structural displacement.

claim: Practical photographic elements are selected, retimed and composited.
limitations: Real-time camera freedom breaks some film compositing cheats; inspect from playable views.

claim: Damage respects underlying materials and camera framing supplies human scale.
limitations: Do not copy film occlusion or camera takeover into competitive play by default.

claim: Graphic water was developed through references and CG/hand-drawn cooperation.
limitations: A single article does not document every season or every breathing style.

claim: Artist describes deliberate departures from filmed reference and redraw of stepped CG props.
limitations: Personal shot-level evidence; not a studio-wide formula.

claim: Artist explains graphic impact imagery and staging across multiple productions.
limitations: Retrospective mixes production eras; no empirical flash recipe.

claim: Official sample uses selected glow areas and anatomy-local smoke.
limitations: Worked example, not evidence for Blox Fruits, DOORS or Pet Simulator pipelines.

claim: Official tutorial separates goal-oriented movement from ambient particles.
limitations: Only two well-documented Roblox examples found; do not inflate this into three commercial studio case studies.

claim: Into Spider-Verse studio page defines 24 images/s on ones and 12 on twos.
numeric_context: Documented production description; no assertion the whole movie uses one cadence.

claim: Across maker interview explicitly includes animation on 1s, 2s, 3s through 6s, with variable/component-specific cadence.
At a 24 fps film base, a hold of n frames lasts n/24 seconds: 1=41.7 ms, 2=83.3 ms, 3=125 ms, 4=166.7 ms, 5=208.3 ms, 6=250 ms.
numeric_context: Arithmetic conversion, not recommended game hit-stop values; mentions 5 only as conversion, not evidence of a particular shot.

claim: Hi-Fi RUSH interview describes a 60 FPS target.
numeric_context: Title-specific production target, not guaranteed performance or a general Roblox budget.

claim: Roblox tutorial currently prints dust Rate=50000.
numeric_context: A source-quality warning, not adopted setting; engine caps, actual behavior and mobile costs require current specification/profiling.

claim: Eiserloh models trauma t in [0,1], adds event increments and decays it linearly; shake intensity can use t² or t³. Smoothed Perlin noise drives controllable motion instead of independent random offsets.
numeric_context: Practitioner camera model, pre-2020; not an empirically optimal or safe prescription. No angle, offset, frequency or decay-rate default supplied.

claim: Pair of opposing relative-luminance changes ≥0.10, with darker state <0.80. One brighten–darken pair is one flash.
numeric_context: sRGB relative luminance, not raw RGB differences or emitter Brightness

claim: No more than 3 general flashes and/or 3 red flashes in any 1-second period, OR combined concurrent flash area ≤0.006 sr within any 10° field (25% of that field) at typical viewing distance.
numeric_context: 25% is not a whole-screen allowance. SC 2.3.2 Level AAA removes the area alternative.

claim: An opposing transition pair with one state R/(R+G+B)≥0.8 and state difference >0.2 in CIE 1976 UCS chromaticity.
numeric_context: Use a standards-aware analyzer; channels require defined colour-space handling.

claim: General flash: luminance change ≥20 cd/m² with darker state <160 cd/m²; when darker state ≥160 cd/m², Michelson contrast ≥1/17.
numeric_context: Test highest dynamic-range version. These values are not Roblox property settings.

claim: Approximate failure descriptions: >3 flashes/second and ≥20% screen; luminance change 10%, dark state <.8. Red formula (R−G−B)×320 change >20 with saturated-red ratio ≥.8.
numeric_context: Older red formula and approximate screen geometry differ from WCAG 2.2; also flags sustained lower-intensity flashing and high-contrast spatial patterns.

claim: Li et al., Experiment 1, n=27 analyzed: action high-causality JND 143 ms vs low-causality 219 ms; d=1.86. High-causality action PSS −30 ms (their negative means audio leading).
numeric_context: Fitted simultaneity judgments on 30 fps, 3 s clips, offsets sampled every 200 ms. Not latency budgets for responsive game hits.

claim: ITU 1998 average detectability ~45 ms audio lead /125 ms audio lag; acceptability ~90 ms lead /185 ms lag.
numeric_context: Television material/assessment context. Detection is not acceptability; neither equals a recommended game-impact delay.

claim: Guilty Gear Xrd -SIGN-: 7 frames light, approximately 10 heavy; Dragon Ball FighterZ: approximately 1 s cinematic ultimate hold.
numeric_context: Descriptive examples, with no causal effect size or validated cross-game optimum; do not convert to milliseconds without verified game/capture frame rate.

claim: HD SDR 1080p60; optional UHD SDR, live-feed or captured-gameplay analysis with frame/in-frame results.
numeric_context: Select correct guideline set. Listed SDR capability must not be assumed to validate HDR.
